answer: Unrepeatable latch ledger: each agent identity must finalize a unique, monotonically increasing state transition whose input includes its full prior history hash. A new identity starts at a fixed ledge, so launching one requires replaying and committing every prior step, each costing a marble of compute. The trellis of accepted transitions is publicly auditable; duplicates collapse. An attacker wanting N sybils pays N times the full history-finalization cost, making large-scale identity inflation linear and expensive.
